pages.text: The $(item)Core Monitor$() is a screen that shows an energy core's numbers from anywhere, even another dimension.$(br2)Place panels facing the same way next to each other: up to 3 by 3 of them join into one bigger screen with more detail. The bottom-left panel draws it.

pages.title: Linking
pages.text: Take a $(item)Crystal Binder$(), Shift-right-click the core (or one of its stabilizers or pylons), then right-click any panel of the screen. All joined panels link at once.$(br2)A core far away only updates while its chunk is loaded; the screen then shows the last values it saw and how long ago.

pages.title: What it shows
pages.text: Fill level with a bar, status (charging, draining, full, low, inactive, stabilizer problem), stored and capacity, energy in and out, the net rate and the time until full or empty. Colours turn yellow below 25% and red below 10%.$(br2)Servers can switch the monitor off with $(l)coreMonitor$() in the config.

pages.title: Settings
pages.text: Right-click a panel with an empty hand for its settings.$(li)$(l)Show$(): which lines the screen shows.$(li)$(l)Core$(): turn the core on or off, preview the next tier.$(li)$(l)Pylons$(): each pylon and its rate; click a mode to switch it.$(li)$(l)Limits$(): max in/out per tick and a reserve %.

pages.title: Look
pages.text: Name the monitor, pick OP, RF, FE or J, set the warning and alarm colours, a target % for the timer, the background, the frame, and a small picture of the core on 2x2 and bigger screens.$(br2)Only the player who linked it (and operators) can change settings.

pages.title: Alerts
pages.text: When the core drops below the alarm %, a stabilizer breaks or the core turns off, the owner gets a chat line, a toast and/or a sound; optionally their FTB Teams party too.$(br2)$(l)Locate$() puts the core's position in chat as a JourneyMap waypoint.

pages.title: Redstone
pages.text: Each panel can give a signal: the fill level (0-15), on below the alarm %, on while full, or on while draining.$(br2)$(l)Stats$() shows the last hour's average and peaks, the lowest fill in 24 hours, and a graph over 5 minutes, 1 hour or 24 hours.

pages.title: Computers
pages.text: With CC: Tweaked the monitor is a peripheral, $(l)draconic_monitor$(): getStored, getCapacity, getPercent, getInput, getOutput, getNet, getEta, getTier, isActive, isLoaded, getLimits and setActive(true/false).
